newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP year net abnormal loss A$976 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP year net abnormal loss A$976 mln.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Friday it had recorded an abnormal loss before tax of A$1.046 billion and an abnormal loss after tax of A$976 million in the year to May 31, 1997.

It said the abnormal losses reflected a write-down in some North American copper assets of A$550 million, a writedown in steel assets of A$220 million, a writedown in minerals assets of A$189 million and a writedown of petroleum assets of A$124 million.
The writedown of petroleum refinery assets was largely offset by the previously announced abnormal profit of A$107 million from the settlement of a tax dispute with the Victorian state government.

The abnormal losses cut BHP's net profit for the year to A$410 million, down 60.8 percent from the 1995/96 result of A$1.O46 billion. The 1995/96 result included a net abnormal loss of A$247 million after tax.
Pre-abnormal profits rose A$93 million to A$1.386 billion, compared with analysts forecasts of between A$1.35 billion to A$1.4 billion.

The return on shareholders equity after abnormal items was 3.3 percent, down from 8.6 percent the previous year, while earnings per share (EPS) after abnormals fell 61.6 percent to 25 cents per share.
The return on shareholders equity excluding abnormals was 11.1 percent, up from 10.7 percent the previous year, while EPS after abnormals rose four cents to 84.5 cents.
BHP said the abnormal loss for copper included a writedown of the value of operating mines in the United States after a strategic review of Magma's performance.
The writedown of steel assets included a charge for plant closures and labour provisions, BHP said.
BHP's shares were up four cents at A$19.10 by 11.33 a.m. (0133 GMT), but up from the A$18.87 plumbed immediately after the result was announced.
